Elena, Irene,

Following up with the technical specifics Greenleaf asked for. High-level summary first, then quick answers to the specific asks: 

Summary:
- Residency: Customers can choose to pin inference routing to EU-only clusters in our Hosted or Dedicated tiers. Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) provide full physical control.
- Transfer mechanism: We support SCCs for EU->US transfers today; Redwood is actively engaged with DPF self-attestation tooling and will provide the DPA annex language that includes SCCs as the primary mechanism with DPF/adequacy fallback language.
- KMS/HSM: We integrate with customer KMS (okta/azure/kms providers) and offer HSM-backed key wrapping for private deployments. Hosted customers may use Redwood-managed keys with optional BYOK.
- Audit logging: We record per-request metadata (timestamp, route, model id, region, token counts) and persist audit logs to an append-only store; logs can be exported in JSON/CSV and we provide a sample schema.

Specifics (short bullets):
- Can EU data be restricted to EU-only? Yes, via routing policy. For Hosted we route to EU clusters; note that auxiliary services (billing, analytics) may process metadata in the US unless explicitly contracted.
- Evidence for KMS/HSM: We will provide architecture diagram + HSM attestation excerpts and the SOC2 section referencing key management controls.
- DPA annex wording: we'll provide a redline-friendly Word doc. Key clause to expect: processor role, authorized subprocessors list, transfers clause (SCCs + DPF fallback), retention and deletion obligations, security measures summary.

I'll collate the SOC2 excerpt and sample logs and post to the shared drive by EOD Friday. Kimberly — can you confirm whether we should propose SCCs only, or SCCs + DPF language for Greenleaf's legal team?

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Principal Privacy Engineer

Elena, team — following up with the materials we discussed. Links and highlights below.

Links provided:
- DPA annex (redline-friendly): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-dpa-drafts (DPA_Annex_Draft_redwood.docx)
- Evidence pack: SOC2 excerpt + sample audit log schema (SOC2_report_redwood_2028.pdf, sample_logs_schema.json)

Quick answers: 
- Suggested export clause (one-paragraph): "Redwood processes Customer Data as a Processor. To the extent Customer Data is transferred outside the EEA, Redwood shall rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (or another approved transfer mechanism) and implement technical and organizational measures consistent with this Annex to protect such transfers. Customer may request EU-only routing where available; auxiliary services may continue to operate in other regions unless otherwise contracted."

- KV/prefix caching: By default our runtime keeps short-lived KV cache to optimize latency. Cache retention is configurable per-customer and can be disabled for Private deployments. For Hosted customers we can set TTLs and provide operational guards; permanent storage of prompt/content is not performed.

- Recommended transfer language for procurement: propose SCCs + DPF fallback (SCCs as contractual guardrail; DPF as additional governance assurance).

Next steps: Irene will send a clean DPA annex draft for Greenleaf legal to redline; David will upload redacted SOC2 pages and the log schema to the drive. If Greenleaf wants more formal attestation (HSM vendor statements, key-wrapping diagrams) we can include those in an appendix.

Please let us know if there are specific line items your legal team expects in the annex — happy to iterate quickly.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Privacy Manager, International Transfers
Redwood Inference
